Article Title: Wall Street's AI jitters return as stocks tumble, S&P500 logs longest losing streak in 2.5 years
Article Text:
Wall Street takes another hit

Anthropic's strong debut fails to lift mood

AI stocks give up early gains as selling returns

AI bubble: Why investors are worried

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Asian markets mixed, European stocks end lower

Wall Street took another hit on Thursday as the AI party appeared to be losing its fizz. US stocks tumbled again as investors continued to dump AI-linked shares, questioning whether the technology's spectacular rally had finally run out of steam.Even Anthropic's blockbuster stock market debut, which saw its shares soar well above the expected price, failed to lift the mood, as worries over sky-high valuations, expensive borrowing and whether massive AI investments will pay off kept investors on edge.The S&P500 fell 2%, marking its sixth straight day of losses. This is its longest losing streak in two and a half years. The index is now 8.2% below the record high it touched last month.The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 1,101.11 points, or 2.2%, while the Nasdaq Composite fell 550.69 points, or 2.3%. The sell-off was broad-based, with more than 90% of the stocks in the S&P500 ending the day lower.The market initially showed signs of recovery after Anthropic, the company behind the Claude AI chatbot, made its stock market debut on Thursday.The company priced its shares at $83 each, higher than its earlier expected range of $70 to $78.Soon after trading began on the Nasdaq shortly before noon, the shares climbed above $115.The strong debut briefly lifted the S&P500 by as much as 1.3%. However, the gains did not last. Anthropic shares eventually closed at $97.17, up 17.1% from their IPO price.The strong demand for the shares showed that investors were still interested in AI companies, despite the recent fall in their stock prices. However, the positive response to Anthropic's listing was not enough to stop the wider market decline.Dan Ives, an analyst at Yorkville Ives, described the current market conditions as “a very turbulent, white-knuckle period.”Several major AI-linked stocks started Thursday's session with gains but later slipped into losses.Micron Technology, which has benefited from rising demand for computer memory because of the AI boom, initially gained 7.8%. However, it reversed course and ended the day 2.1% lower.CoreWeave, which buys AI chips and rents access to them to customers through the cloud, also saw its shares swing sharply. After rising 10.5% in the morning, the stock ended the session down 6.1%.Nvidia shares followed a similar pattern. The stock erased its early gain of 4.7% and closed 3.3% lower as concerns about the AI industry continued to weigh on investors.The recent fall in AI stocks comes amid growing concerns about whether their high prices can be justified.One of the biggest worries is that shares of AI companies may have become too expensive after their sharp rise. Investors are also questioning whether AI will generate enough profits and improve productivity enough to justify the huge amounts companies are spending on data centres.High interest rates have added to these concerns. With borrowing becoming more expensive, investors fear that companies may find it harder to raise the money needed to expand their AI businesses.Political developments have also added to the uncertainty. Sweeping victories for Democrats in the US midterm elections this month have raised concerns that AI companies could face more regulations.Another development adding to the concerns was the sudden resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Huang was one of the biggest supporters of the AI industry and helped build investor interest in the technology. He also used some of Nvidia's huge profits to support the industry's growth.In the bond market, US treasury yields declined as investors moved towards investments considered safer amid the fall in stock prices.The yield on the 10-year US Treasury slipped to 5.04% from 5.07% on Wednesday. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions, so when bond prices rise, their yields fall.Elsewhere, stock markets remained mixed.Japan's Nikkei 225 rose 0.7%, helped by a 4.6% gain in SoftBank Group. The company was an early investor in OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT and a competitor to Anthropic.South Korea's Kospi also gained 1.4%, supported by a rise in stocks linked to the AI boom.However, stocks were weaker in other parts of Asia and Europe. Germany's DAX fell 1.1%.At the end of Thursday's trading session, the S&P 500 dropped 147.80 points to 7,175.83. The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 1,101.11 points to close at 49,097.06, while the Nasdaq Composite fell 550.69 points to 23,879.20.
Article Summary: The S&P500 fell 2%, marking its sixth straight day of losses. This is its longest losing streak in two and a half years. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 1,101.11 points, or 2.2%. Even Anthropic's blockbuster stock market debut failed to lift the mood.

Article Title: Go public or stay private: Tata Sons gears up for decision this week
Article Text:
Board will take up disputed minutes of Sept 17 meeting where N Chandrasekaran (R) was reappointed chairman by 4–1 vote, with Noel Tata (L) opposing

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

MUMBAI: Tata Sons is heading into one of its most consequential weeks in decades. When its board meets on November 26, it will confront a choice that could determine whether the Tata Group's closely held holding company remains private or opens its doors to the public.It has to pick between two competing paths: RBI 's Nov 16 letter reiterating that Tata Sons must comply with rules governing upper-layer non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) to list its shares, and Tata Trusts' Sept 28 proposal to merge two companies into Tata Sons, which would take the combined entity outside the NBFC and core investment company (CIC) framework and avoid a listing.The six-member board is already divided, with Trusts chairman Noel Tata, a director of Tata Sons, opposed to an IPO while the other five directors favour compliance with RBI's listing requirement. The divide extends to Trusts, where trustees including Noel's older half-brother Jimmy Tata, Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh, are in favour of an IPO.RBI's latest missive and Trusts' merger plan both followed the dramatic Sept 17 Tata Sons board meet, where almost all directors argued in favour of compliance.Noel, however, maintained that compliance need not mean a listing and the company should examine alternatives.The RBI letter makes no reference to the merger proposal, but it refers to the Tata Sons board meeting and says it understood the company's Oct 6 request for guidance on listing. Noel has questioned whether Tata Sons has sought the RBI's guidance on his merger proposal and asked the company to evaluate it and present its pros and cons to the board this week.Senior advocate Harish Salve who advises Tata Sons and chairman N Chandrasekaran has publicly endorsed a listing. "If the RBI says go list yourself, there is no use saying my shareholders don't agree," he said, maintaining that going public would bring greater transparency and prevent the company from being paralysed by disagreements among Tata Trusts trustees.Senior advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi, representing Trusts, has argued for their primacy as Tata Sons' controlling shareholder. He said the company cannot have a "runaway board" taking major decisions in disagreement with the Trusts. Tata Sons is the only company among the relevant upper-layer NBFCs to remain unlisted.If both items are put to a vote, the outcome is expected to be 5:1 in each case, but with Noel being in a minority: voting against an IPO and in favour of the Trusts' merger proposal. That, however, would reopen the dispute over Article 121 of Tata Sons' Articles of Association.Noel's position is that a resolution under Article 121 must secure the affirmative vote of a majority of Trust-nominated directors. With Noel and Srinivasan as the two Trust nominees, the Trusts contend that both must vote in favour. Tata Sons disputes this interpretation, maintaining that if the two Trust nominees vote in opposite directions, Article 121 allows the chairman of the meeting to exercise a casting vote to break the tie. It relied on precisely that interpretation at the Sept 17 meeting, when Noel opposed Chandrasekaran's reappointment and Srinivasan supported it.Also on Thursday's agenda is the Shapoorji Pallonji (SP) Group's proposal to monetise part of its 18.4% holding in Tata Sons for Rs 25,000 crore, a transaction that would alter the holding company's shareholding structure. Noel has proposed that it be implemented through a selective reduction of capital, with the shares valued under rule 11UA of the Income Tax Rules. Chandrasekaran is expected to present the board with an assessment of how Tata Sons would fund the payout, including through internal cash flows, the sale of listed investments or stake sales in newer businesses.The listing, merger and SP proposals are among seven items on the agenda. Others include dematerialisation of Tata Sons shares, including holdings of Trusts and Ratan Tata; consideration of the company's second-quarter FY27 results; business reviews of Agratas (battery venture), Tata AIG General Insurance, Tejas Networks (telecom equipment) and Air India; and a review of Tata Sons' guarantees and investments.But first the board will take up disputed minutes of Sept 17 meeting. Noel expects his objections, including his dissent over Chandrasekaran's reappointment and his interpretation of Article 121 to be reflected in the final record. Once final minutes are signed by Chandrasekaran, the board will turn to the proposals, with India Inc watching closely.
Article Summary: Tata Sons' board will confront a choice that could determine whether the Tata Group's closely held holding company remains private or opens its doors to the public. Board will take up disputed minutes of Sept 17 meeting where N Chandrasekaran was reappointed chairman by 4–1 vote. Trusts chairman Noel Tata, a director of Tata Sons, opposed to an IPO.

Article Title: No invite for China at Anthropic IPO: After SpaceX, Claude parent too shuts Chinese investors out
Article Text:
Anthropic IPO

Why keep Chinese investors at arm's length?

Trump and Xi may be talking, but technology remains a sticking point

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Everyone wants a slice of the AI bigfoot, but where you come from could decide whether you get one!Earlier billionaire Elon Musk's AI and aerospace giant SpaceX barred investors from Hong Kong and mainland China from buying its shares. Now, Anthropic followed a similar route. While the IPO was open only to investors from selected countries, the repeated exclusion of Chinese investors by major US technology companies raises questions.The artificial intelligence company behind the Claude chatbot reportedly turned away investment from Chinese and Hong Kong firms ahead of its public listing, in what went on to record as the biggest initial public offering (IPO) in history.Three people familiar with the decision said Anthropic had excluded investors from the two regions, New York Times reported.The move comes amid growing US efforts to restrict China's access to advanced artificial intelligence technology. As Washington and Beijing compete for supremacy in AI, technology and investment are increasingly becoming flashpoints in their already strained relationship.The exclusion comes against the backdrop of a growing technology rivalry between the US and China.The Trump administration has been taking steps to restrict China's access to advanced AI technology, while both countries are drawing red lines around their homegrown technologies.Anthropic's decision appears in line with a wider trend among major American technology companies. SpaceX and its bankers had taken a similar step ahead of the company's blockbuster IPO in July, shutting Chinese investors out of the offering.OpenAI, another leading AI company, is also expected to bar Chinese investors from its eventual public listing. It has already prevented investors from China from participating in its private fund-raising rounds.There is another common thread connecting all three companies: Anthropic, SpaceX and OpenAI have all counted the US government among their clients.The decision also comes at an interesting moment in US-China relations. US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping met on Thursday at the APEC meeting in Shenzhen, China, with both leaders looking to bring some stability and goodwill into an increasingly rocky economic relationship.During the meeting, Xi called on members to build an "open ecosystem" for technology. Yet, while the two leaders are attempting to improve ties, their governments continue to build barriers around trade, technology and capital.The latest developments around AI chips underline just how difficult that balancing act is. Hours before Trump arrived in Asia for meetings with regional leaders, his administration moved to restrict China's access to advanced artificial intelligence chips.Beijing was quick to warn that it could respond with countermeasures if Washington continued with the restrictions."If the US persists, China will take countermeasures," China warned.A spokesman for China's Ministry of Commerce also expressed strong opposition to the latest US measures on Thursday."China is deeply concerned about — and firmly opposes — a series of recent economic and trade restrictive measures taken by the US against China," the spokesman told NYT.The latest restrictions on artificial intelligence are adding to a series of escalating moves by both countries. China experts have warned that the new AI rule could make it harder for Trump and Xi to reach any meaningful agreement to ease tensions.
Article Summary: Anthropic turned away Chinese and Hong Kong investors ahead of its IPO. Elon Musk's SpaceX also barred Chinese investors from its IPO in July. The move comes amid growing US efforts to restrict China's access to advanced artificial intelligence technology. Technology and investment are increasingly becoming flashpoints in US-China relations.

Article Title: Gold price crash: From Rs 1.80 lakh to below Rs 1.25 lakh, will gold now plunge to Rs 1 lakh per 10 gms?
Article Text:
Till a few weeks ago, a fall to Rs 1.25 lakh levels seemed unlikely, but that level too has been breached

Why has gold been crashing in 2026?

So, is there an end in sight to this fall? What should investors do, and does the crash mean that gold has lost its safe haven appeal. We ask experts:

Will gold fall to Rs 1 lakh per 10 grams?

What Jateen Trivedi said

Has gold lost its safe haven status?

What Manav Modi said

What should investors do and what’s the outlook for 2027?

What Maneesh Sharma said

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)

Gold is no longer glittery or shining - in fact gold prices have crashed around 33% from the highs seen in India earlier this year. In 2025, there seemed no end in sight for gold’s spectacular rally. Come 2026, the year started with the yellow metal hitting a lifetime high of Rs 1.8 lakh per 10 grams in futures contract.And then the story went downhill - with no immediate bottom in sight!In the international markets, gold has dropped roughly 37% to around $3,527 per ounce, its lowest level in over a year. In India, MCX gold November futures recently slipped to around Rs 1,21,424 per 10 grams. The crash has been relatively less in India because the government hiked customs duty on gold and silver earlier this year, cushioning the fall to some extent.Gold started falling in January as investors booked profit, but before it could find its equilibrium, the US-Iran war triggered another crash.Analysts say that the recent decline reflects a combination of profit-booking, liquidation of leveraged positions, changing interest-rate expectations and a stronger dollar.Key reasons for such a sharp fall include recent equity and tech-stock pullbacks, where investors sold liquid gold positions to raise cash or meet margin calls rather than using it as a shield while elevated bond yields and expectations of tighter interest rates in the US raised the opportunity cost of holding gold.Till a few weeks ago, a fall to Rs 1.25 lakh levels seemed unlikely, but that level too has been breached. So, does that mean that there is a chance of gold prices falling to Rs 1 lakh per 10 grams as well?Experts don’t rule out the possibility, though they believe that underlying fundamentals of gold such as central bank buying will continue to support the yellow metal. This indicates that a further fall may not sustain for long, they say.Jateen Trivedi, VP Research Analyst - Commodity and Currency, LKP Securities says, “A decline towards Rs 1,00,000 cannot be ruled out if the rupee appreciates significantly and COMEX Gold corrects towards $3,000.”“However, the more important question is whether such lower levels can sustain and establish a long-term base. Given rapidly changing global investment themes and persistent geopolitical uncertainty, I do not expect prices to sustain below Rs 1,15,000 for long,” Trivedi tells TOI.Manav Modi, Commodities Analyst at Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd says, “The breach of Rs 1.25 lakh highlights how quickly sentiment and price expectations can change in a highly volatile market.”But, the analyst notes that a fall towards Rs 1 lakh would require a deeper strength in story as well positioning, potentially driven by sustained dollar strength, higher real yields, continued speculative unwinding and a moderation in investment demand.“However, the extent of the recent correction also needs to be assessed against gold’s underlying physical and central bank demand, which remains an important structural support,” he tells TOI.Commodity analyst Maneesh Sharma says that technically, the spot gold pair has extended a bearish phase following the recent breakdown below the previous consolidation phase.Moreover, the yellow metal holds well below the technically significant 200-day Simple Moving Average (SMA) validating the negative outlook.“While oversold technical indicators like RSI indicate that downside pace could slow but not yet reverse the trend. Having said that, a near term consolidation is still possible but could not stop the extension of a recent well established downtrend making gold vulnerable to fall further up to $3420-3380 / Oz in Spot (CMP $ 3575/Oz). On MCX futures, a sustainable close below Rs. 1,21,000/10 gm could accelerate its downtrend towards Rs. 1,18,000-1,16,000/10 gm on MCX,” he tells TOI.No.Jateen Trivedi of LKP Securities believes that even though gold has witnessed a sharp correction, this does not mean it has lost its safe-haven status.“If we look at the two-year performance, prices have risen from around Rs 75,000 in January 2025 to nearly Rs 1,25,000 currently, delivering returns of approximately 55%,” Trivedi points out.“An asset that has preserved value for over 5,000 years will inevitably experience cycles of profit booking and corrections. Gold's safe-haven appeal remains intact; recent weakness reflects changing market dynamics rather than a loss of its investment relevance,” he adds.Commodity analyst Maneesh Sharma is of the view that gold’s long term role as a monetary and currency hedge still remains intact as long-term drivers like central bank buying and sovereign debt concerns remain relevant over time.But, Manav Modi cautions that while gold may not have lost its appeal as a safe haven asset, the recent price movements highlight that it is not immune to sharp corrections, particularly when speculative positioning becomes stretched.“Safe haven demand can also take a backseat when investors prioritise liquidity and reduce exposure across asset classes. Gold’s underlying role as a portfolio diversifier and reserve asset remains intact,” he tells TOI.Gold continues to be supported by central bank buying and recently ETF inflows. According to the latest World Gold Council report, Central bank buying jumped to 321t in Q3, eclipsing recent typical quarterly buying levels and lifting ytd demand to 675t. Gold ETFs reversed course following the Q2 outflows, adding 211t in Q3.So if the yellow metal continues to be a safe haven asset, what should your investment strategy in the current situation be?Experts believe the ongoing correction can be a good opportunity to accumulate gold, though cautiously and keeping your overall portfolio balance in mind.“This correction offers an opportunity to review gold allocation rather than panic over falling prices or focus on previous highs near Rs 1,80,000,” Jateen Trivedi says.“Investors should evaluate their overall portfolio allocation and consider staggered accumulation. Those with less than 15% allocation to gold may consider adding gradually, including a small lump-sum investment if significantly underinvested. The focus should be on long-term portfolio diversification rather than timing the exact bottom,” he recommends.Manav Modi recommends a staggered strategy to accumulate gold. “But, since further downside cannot be ignored, post some clarity, accumulation could be looked at,” he says.Finally, where is gold headed in 2027?Maneesh Sharma shares that a 20-25% recovery to around $4500/Oz still looks possible in the second half of 2027 considering continued central-bank purchase & broader ETF inflows would strengthen support which translates to a level of Rs 1,45,000-1,50,000/10 gm on MCX futures contract.Jateen Trivedi too believes that gold could move towards Rs 1,55,000-Rs 1,65,000 over the next year, depending on international prices and the rupee's trajectory.“COMEX Gold could potentially revisit the $4,500 zone, supported by central-bank demand and geopolitical uncertainty. However, continued rupee appreciation could limit domestic gains, resulting in Indian gold underperforming international prices,” he says.
Article Summary: Gold prices have crashed around 33% from the highs seen in India earlier this year. In the international markets, gold has dropped roughly 37% to around $3,527 per ounce. In India, MCX gold November futures recently slipped to around Rs 1,21,424 per 10 grams. Key reasons for such a sharp fall include recent equity and tech-stock pullbacks.

Article Title: Record Rs 1.22 lakh crore foreign inflows: Is India becoming the world's 'anti-AI' trade?
Article Text:
Since the US-mid term elections, the selloff in AI-related stocks has intensified. In contrast, India has seen record foreign investor inflows in the month of November.

What is fueling the Indian stock market rally?

Which sectors are expected to benefit?

What’s the outlook?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Inflation and rates. CPI rose above the RBI’s 6% upper limit in September, a two-year high, signaling another rate hike. Banks, which are heavily weighted in the index and in FPI buying, are the sensitive point.

AI-trade rebound. A recovery in AI-related stocks could redirect money back to overseas tech markets. This is the biggest swing factor, since the inflow is largely the mirror image of the AI outflow.

Crude and the rupee. Rising crude, persistent global volatility and a reversal in foreign inflows are the obvious risks.

Policy disappointment. Some of the rally reflects hopes of LTCG tax relief, which is a risk if it doesn’t come.

Domestic support. DII selling (which has been noticed) into strength means less of a cushion if FPIs pause.

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)

Was the artificial intelligence (AI)-led stock rally a bubble all along? Has it burst? And, is India which suffered sharp foreign outflows over the last two years for the lack of an AI story, now becoming the new favourite? Is India the world’s ‘anti-AI’ trade?Global stock markets tell a revealing story: Since the US-mid term elections, the selloff in AI-related stocks has intensified, exacerbated by the unfolding crisis at Nvidia. Since then, Nasdaq is down 7.98%. South Korea’s Kospi and Taiwan’s TAIEX - the proxies for AI trade in Asia are down 3.74% and 9.24% respectively.In contrast, India has seen record foreign investor inflows in the month of November. Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) have remained net buyers on every trading day this month, barring the Muhurat trading session. Their cumulative purchases reached Rs 1.22 lakh crore by November 20, according to CDSL, which marks an all-time high! Sensex has risen 10.87% in November and 3.57% since the US mid-term results.The shift in FPI flows appears to indicate a broader reallocation of investments away from AI and AI-linked stocks towards India’s diversified equity market. The buying trend is expected to persist in the near term.Analysts believe that India is increasingly becoming a natural alternative for growth-focused investors seeking to diversify their exposure, as enthusiasm on Wall Street for Asian stocks linked to artificial intelligence, particularly in South Korea and Taiwan, begins to fade.India’s large market and wide range of investment opportunities are helping it emerge as a potential hedge for investors.Experts believe that while India may not be a conventional safe haven, its strong domestic consumption, policy stability, resilient financial system and improving earnings outlook offer a compelling investment proposition.According to Somil Mehta, Head of Retail Research at Mirae Asset Sharekhan, India is emerging as an alternative destination for global investors who are now actively reducing their exposure to expensive AI-linked stocks.“India’s relatively lower exposure to the global AI trade, large domestic market, resilient economy and improving corporate earnings are attracting interest. However, this is a relative safe-haven opportunity, not complete protection from global volatility,” Mehta tells TOI.Arun Kailasan, Research Analyst, Geojit Investments Limited echoes the sentiment: the ongoing rally reflects a relative reallocation of capital rather than a safe-haven trade.As stretched AI-linked valuations unwind, foreign investors are moving towards markets with domestically anchored earnings.India's limited exposure to AI hardware, resilient consumption, sustained public capex and macroeconomic stability support this shift.“In addition, segments where valuations moderated after the recent correction are now attracting fresh foreign inflows,” he tells TOI.However, Utsav Verma, Head of Research at Choice Institutional Equities cautions that the rally is mostly a foreign-led rotation out of the AI trade, helped by cheaper crude and better earnings. Domestic institutions were net sellers into it.“I’d treat it as tactical for now. A structural rerating would need the flows to last for several quarters,” he says.Ajit Mishra, SVP- Research, Religare Broking is of the view that a sustained shift in global capital towards India could benefit sectors with strong domestic growth visibility, particularly banking and financials, automobiles, capital goods, power, pharmaceuticals and consumption.“Stocks such as HDFC Bank, Kotak Bank, Mahindra & Mahindra, Larsen & Toubro, Power Grid and Reliance Industries offer exposure to India's domestic investment and consumption cycle and could attract greater institutional interest,” he tells TOI.“Indian IT services may witness some near-term volatility as global investors reassess AI-led disruption and technology spending. However, established IT companies with strong client relationships and capabilities in digital transformation could also benefit from the broader adoption of AI over the medium term,” he adds.Aamar Deo Singh, Head - Research, Angel One also sees ⁠financials, consumption and capital goods gaining the most, along with telecom and autos, as these run on domestic demand and have nothing to do with the AI cycle, and such money in any case goes first to liquid large caps.“IT services is the tricky one, the rotation helps for now but AI is asking hard questions of its business. The names which ran up here on the AI theme may have to give back some gains,” he says.It’s important to understand that India’s outperformance reflects both improving domestic fundamentals and a shift in global investment flows. Better corporate earnings, domestic consumption and infrastructure spending provide support.Tanvi Kanchan, Associate Director, Anand Rathi Share and Stock Brokers Limited points out that India’s outperformance has a firmer floor this time because of earnings and valuations but the pace of the past month has been driven by global positioning, and that component will stay volatile.But as Somil Mehta cautions: foreign investor buying has also contributed significantly to the rally. If global sentiment changes, these flows could reverse. Sustainable gains will ultimately depend on earnings growth.But he believes that the underlying strength of the rally reflects a certain durability.Corporate earnings growth remains steady. Banking balance sheets are healthy, with improved asset quality and adequate capital buffers. Corporate leverage is contained. Sustained domestic institutional and retail inflows further reduce the market's reliance on foreign capital.“The sustainability of this outperformance, however, will ultimately depend on whether corporate earnings growth remains strong enough to justify current valuations and support continued investor confidence,” he tells TOI.Utsav Verma of Choice Institutional Equities sums it up: India’s relative strength has been noticed. India is being used as a hedge against AI concentration, and its underweight positioning has amplified the move.According to him, some key monitorables in the next few weeks are:
Article Summary: Since the US-mid term elections, the selloff in AI-related stocks has intensified. In contrast, India has seen record foreign investor inflows in the month of November. Analysts believe that India is increasingly becoming a natural alternative for growth-focused investors seeking to diversify their exposure.

New Delhi even suggested to discuss tariffs first and postpone more difficult market access issues. The plan to purchase $500 billion worth of US products over five years gave American exporters an interest in the negotiations' result. Rohit Kumar Singh, Eminence Strategy Consulting Pvt Ltd

US wants greater access to 140 crore buyers

Manufacturing and supply chain

America's exports to India (Credit: IBEF)

Strategic partnership

India, a strategic counterweight to China

For the US, India is not just a trading partner but a crucial alternative for diversifying global supply chains and reducing overdependence on a few countries...America recognises India's importance, and any serious global economic strategy today must have India at its centre. Jagvinder Singh Virk, Global Affairs & Geopolitics Expert

India's approach: Firm on its terms, open to flexibility

India-US trade bilateral trade

What's next for India?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Indians have always loved a good bargain, whether it is haggling over daily groceries or negotiating a trade deal with another country. After all, it is not a deal until you know you have secured better terms than the next person in line!After months of trade negotiations, the US has agreed to give India a comparative tariff advantage over peer economies under the proposed bilateral trade pact. However, the deal is yet to be signed.Earlier on Wednesday, India said it could sign the agreement only after the new tariff framework is in place and investigations under Section 301 are concluded.The India-US trade deal has seen several twists and turns since negotiations began in February 2025, from tariff threats and hopes of an agreement to a sudden courtroom setback. Now, with the deal back on the table, the latest development has raised a key question: What has changed, and why is the US suddenly offering the 'tariff king' a better deal?The two sides had finalised the first tranche of the pact, which proposed an additional 18% tariff on Indian exports. However, the US Supreme Court's decision to strike down the "reciprocal tariffs" put the agreement on hold.Now, Washington's willingness to give India a comparative tariff advantage over its peers has brought the negotiations back into focus.India's importance to Washington goes well beyond trade figures. Its vast consumer market, supply of affordable medicines and potential to emerge as an alternative manufacturing base to China give the US several reasons to keep the partnership strong.Tariff competitiveness is another important part of the equation. When the first-phase BTA framework was finalised, India enjoyed a tariff advantage over ASEAN nations — Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, the Philippines, Brunei, Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar and Cambodia — as well as Sri Lanka, Pakistan and Bangladesh.But a lower tariff does not always mean a better deal.If India's rivals secure bigger tariff cuts, their products could become cheaper in the US market, leaving Indian exporters struggling to compete. The real advantage, therefore, lies not just in lower duties but in ensuring that India remains ahead of its competitors.So, what makes India a partner Washington cannot afford to overlook?India's importance to the US goes beyond trade, particularly when it comes to medicines. The country supplies 47% of US generic prescription drugs and 60% of hypertension medicines. Steep tariffs could hit American consumers and patients first.Rohit Kumar Singh of Eminence Strategy Consulting warns, “Disruption in supply might impact American citizens directly.”Replacing approved manufacturers, he adds, takes both investment and time.Even when the US threatened a 100% tariff on pharmaceutical imports, India remained largely shielded. Generics account for over 90% of medicines used in America and were exempted to avoid shortages and price spikes.Similarly, under the February 6 framework, the US had proposed scrapping reciprocal tariffs on Indian generics and their ingredients, with further concessions subject to a separate US investigation.The proposed purchases under the interim trade framework also give American businesses a reason to support closer trade ties with India.Under an earlier statement, India had indicated its intention to purchase $500 billion worth of US products over five years. These included energy products, aircraft and aircraft parts, precious metals, technology products and coking coal.For perspective, India's imports from all countries stood at $527.21 billion during April-October 2026-27.Singh adds that pushing India too hard could jeopardise these potential sales.As Sandeep Gupta of Executive Access sums it up, “It’s a ‘we can scratch each other’s back effectively’ deal that works for both sides.”With over 140 crore people, India is a shopper's paradise for American brands. Nearly 65% of Indians are under 35, and rising household incomes are expected to drive demand across categories, from appliances and cars to IT services. This creates opportunities for American companies selling technology, parts and financing.Geopolitics expert Jagvinder Singh Virk told TOI, “This young demographic, our expanding middle class, growing purchasing power and rapidly developing economy make India one of the most attractive markets in the world.”The US already sold India $45.4 billion worth of goods and $42.9 billion worth of services in 2025, according to USTR. Walking away from the partnership could mean losing access to an expanding market and future customers.Global companies do not just want to sell in India; they also want to manufacture here and benefit from its growth.Virk says, “India is also emerging as a trusted global manufacturing and supply-chain partner.”Despite a bumpy global economic environment, India's exports grew over 16% in the first seven months of FY 2026-27.The US increasingly sees India as a strategic economic partner rather than just another trading destination. Its willingness to offer the country a tariff advantage over competing economies also reflects India's growing bargaining power in trade negotiations.India-US relations extend beyond trade, with both countries sharing strategic interests in the Indo-Pacific region.One example is the Quad, comprising India, the US, Japan and Australia, which focuses on cooperation in maritime security and critical technologies. In May 2026, the four countries launched an Indo-Pacific maritime surveillance project and a framework to strengthen critical-mineral supply chains.Singh cautions that any weakening of this partnership “will make it harder to implement plans to develop alternatives to concentrated supply networks.”Ritik Bhandari, team lead, Centre for Law, Policy and Governance, NFPRC Foundation says that India's growing importance to the US is driven by both economic opportunities and shared strategic interests.He further points out that India offers Washington a large consumer base, manufacturing capabilities and scope for collaboration in technology and energy. Its role in diversifying global supply chains and strengthening the US presence in the Indo-Pacific further adds to its importance.The proposed tariff advantage, he says, reflects Washington's intention to ensure India remains competitive against other trading partners.For years, China has been America's factory floor, supplying everything from electronics to industrial components. But Washington is now looking to reduce that dependence, and India is emerging as an important alternative.Gupta said, “The US wants to reduce its dependence on China-dominated manufacturing items such as electronics, pharmaceuticals, minerals and manufacturing, which India can effectively offer.”US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer echoed this view in an interview with Fox News, acknowledging that “India can be a way station for that.”Losing India's trust, therefore, could prove costly for Washington on two fronts. American exporters risk losing access to Indian consumers, while US manufacturers could find themselves with fewer alternatives to Chinese suppliers.India has made it clear that a trade deal cannot come at any cost. Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman had earlier said negotiations had reached a stage where further give-and-take would be “very, very difficult”, describing the pact as a “hard and very vigorously negotiated agreement”.Both countries, however, maintain that they are working towards a fair and mutually beneficial deal. US embassy deputy chief of mission Jason Meeks recently described the proposed partnership as “fair, reciprocal, and mutually beneficial”, with cooperation extending beyond goods.According to Jagvinder Singh Virk, India changed the tone of negotiations with “a clear economic vision, well-defined priorities and a willingness to find practical solutions”. New Delhi, he said, had shown that it could protect its core interests while remaining flexible where both sides stood to gain.Washington, too, has reasons not to push too hard. India offers US companies a vast consumer market, a young workforce, growing manufacturing capabilities and an opportunity to diversify supply chains.Comparing the talks with negotiations involving Canada and South Korea, Virk said India's growing economic strength and strategic importance set it apart.India, meanwhile, remains firm on sensitive sectors such as agriculture and dairy. It is open to a deal, but wants one that safeguards its interests and recognises its growing economic role.India-US ties may finally be turning a corner.Chief economic adviser V Anantha Nageswaran said recent weeks had shown signs of easing tensions, adding that a trade deal in early December could mean “we may have seen the worst of the unsettled phase behind us”.One of the bigger questions is whether the agreement can help India reduce its dependence on China. Initiatives such as Make in India, the PLI scheme and Aatmanirbhar Bharat offer a starting point. However, India must build its own manufacturing capabilities rather than simply replace dependence on China with dependence on the US.The next step, therefore, is to strengthen domestic capacity. Bhandari added that manufacturing incentives could encourage Indian companies to produce more raw materials at home, while long-term US orders could help fund these facilities."The government's focus on domestic manufacturing, infrastructure development and initiatives such as Make in India and the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme provides a strong foundation for this transition. Importantly, India is approaching this partnership from a position of strategic autonomy, seeking to expand international economic cooperation while strengthening its domestic capabilities.This is an opportunity to reinforce India's economic resilience and global standing," Bhandari said.At the same time, India needs to find alternative sources for critical inputs. The real opportunity is not just to become an alternative to China, but to emerge as a manufacturing and technology powerhouse in its own right.
Article Summary: After months of trade negotiations, the US has agreed to give India a comparative tariff advantage over peer economies. The two sides had finalised the first tranche of the pact, which proposed an additional 18% tariff on Indian exports. But the US Supreme Court's decision to strike down the "reciprocal tariffs" put the agreement on hold.

Article Title: Rupee snaps five-day winning streak, falls 23 paise to 92.85 against US dollar
Article Text:
Rupee ends five-day winning run as dollar firms, equities fall

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The rupee snapped its five-session winning streak on Monday after touching a seven-month high, as corporate demand for dollars and weakness in domestic equities offset support from strong foreign portfolio inflows.The currency climbed to around 92.43-92.44 against the US dollar in early trade, its strongest level since April, before reversing direction. It was trading at 92.85 in early trade, down 23 paise from its previous close, according to PTI. Reuters later quoted the rupee at 92.8825, compared with its previous close of 92.67.The retreat came after a sharp rally over the past week. The rupee had gained 70 paise on Friday to close at 92.62, moving above the 93 mark for the first time since April 10. It had strengthened more than 1.6% over five consecutive sessions from its November 13 close of 94.19.The currency's recovery has been supported by strong foreign portfolio inflows into Indian equities. Overseas investors have poured about $13 billion into domestic stocks so far in November, according to Reuters, amid a global rotation away from crowded artificial intelligence trades.However, traders said a burst of corporate dollar buying weighed on the rupee after its early gains, with demand reportedly coming from two large conglomerates.The currency's rapid appreciation had also pushed it into overbought territory, according to a key momentum indicator.Goldman Sachs described the rupee as a “port of stability in the AI storm”, saying the currency had benefited from the broader shift in global market positioning.The brokerage, however, cautioned that the pace of appreciation may not be sustainable, given India's need to rebuild its external reserve buffers. It said there appeared to be a greater willingness to allow two-way volatility in the currency.India's foreign exchange reserves fell by $14.205 billion to $705.342 billion in the week ended November 13, according to Reserve Bank of India data, taking them to a three-month low.The dollar index was down 0.03% at 103.71, while Brent crude futures fell 0.28% to $92.38 a barrel.Domestic equities were lower in early trade, with the Sensex falling 0.49% and the Nifty declining 0.46%. Foreign institutional investors had bought equities worth Rs 10,308.42 crore on a net basis on Friday, according to exchange data.The rupee has also strengthened against other major currencies in November, gaining around 4% against the British pound and the euro and 3% against the Japanese yen, Reuters reported.
Article Summary: Rupee snapped its five-session winning streak on Monday after touching a seven- month high. The currency climbed to around 92.43-92.44 against the US dollar in early trade, its strongest level since April, before reversing direction. The retreat came after a sharp rally over the past week.

Article Title: India, Vietnam to lead Asia-Pacific growth in 2027 as China slows: S&P
Article Text:
Representative image

El Nino, rising costs pose inflation risks

Asia-Pacific growth to moderate, China remains weak spot

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India's economy is expected to grow by 7 per cent in both the current and the next financial years, keeping the country among the fastest-growing economies in the Asia-Pacific region in 2027, according to S&P Global Ratings.In its Economic Outlook for Asia-Pacific, released on Monday, the rating agency said India and Vietnam were likely to lead regional growth next year, with Vietnam's economy projected to expand by 7.5 per cent.China's growth, meanwhile, is expected to slow to 4.3 per cent in 2027 from 4.5 per cent in 2026.S&P said India's expansion during the June and September quarters was supported by strong goods exports, public-sector investment and household consumption, with the latter benefiting from buoyant credit growth."We expect Vietnam and India to be the region's fastest-growing economies in 2027," the agency said.India's export performance has benefited from higher commodity prices, trade diversification and its growing integration into global supply chains. S&P said the strength was particularly visible in electronic and engineering goods, as well as chemicals.Despite the strong growth outlook, S&P expects India's growth-inflation mix to become less favourable in the second half of the current financial year, as higher input costs are increasingly passed on to consumers.It flagged uneven monsoon conditions, deficient summer rainfall and lower reservoir levels as factors that could weigh on current agricultural output and the upcoming winter crop. Persistent El Nino conditions are also expected to put pressure on food prices across Asia-Pacific, particularly in India.The agency expects inflation in India to average 5.3 per cent in the financial year ending March 2027, with risks tilted to the upside.Retail inflation stood at 6.1 per cent in October, breaching the Reserve Bank of India 's tolerance band of 2-6 per cent.S&P anticipates a further 25-basis-point policy rate hike by the RBI in December, followed by another increase in early 2027. It expects inflation to ease to 4.7 per cent in the financial year ending March 2028.India is scheduled to release its official GDP growth data for the July-September quarter on November 30.The RBI had projected 7.2 per cent growth for the quarter, while the Finance Ministry's Monthly Economic Review estimated it at 7.35 per cent.At the regional level, S&P expects Asia-Pacific economic growth to ease to 4.4 per cent in 2027 from 4.8 per cent in 2026. It identified high energy prices as the biggest macroeconomic headwind and the global expansion of artificial intelligence infrastructure as the largest growth tailwind, although both forces are expected to moderate somewhat next year.The agency expects exports to remain strong, largely driven by shipments of AI-related technology, while domestic demand is likely to stay broadly resilient outside China.However, it warned that technology export growth could peak in the coming quarters because of challenging base effects and a possible slowdown in AI infrastructure investment in the US and other markets.China is expected to remain a weak spot in the regional outlook, with S&P projecting its growth to slow to 4.3 per cent in 2027 from 4.5 per cent this year.The agency cited weak domestic demand, a prolonged downturn in the housing sector and subdued consumption and investment.It also said the likelihood of significant fresh policy stimulus in China was limited, given that the country's 2026 growth target of 4.5 per cent was within reach.S&P identified three major risks to the regional outlook: a significant slowdown in global AI-related spending, persistently high energy prices and a sharper increase in global interest rates.While consumer inflation across Asia-Pacific is expected to moderate in 2027 as the impact of higher energy prices eases, the agency cautioned that prolonged high energy costs could push inflation and interest rates higher.Stronger pressure from US interest rates could also trigger capital outflows and currency depreciation in some economies.
Article Summary: India and Vietnam likely to lead regional growth next year, with Vietnam's economy projected to expand by 7.5%. China's growth, meanwhile, is expected to slow to 4.3 per cent in 2027 from 4.5 per cent this year. Persistent El Nino conditions are also expected to put pressure on food prices across Asia-Pacific.

Article Title: Tata Steel to acquire 26.6% promoter stake in APL Apollo for Rs 15,510 crore
Article Text:
Tata Steel to acquire 26.6% stake in APL Apollo for Rs 15,510 crore and launch a 26% open offer.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Tata Steel on Monday announced that it has entered into an agreement to acquire a 26.6% promoter stake in APL Apollo Tubes Ltd for Rs 15,510 crore at Rs 2,100 per share. The company will subsequently launch an open offer to acquire an additional 26% stake at Rs 2,301.40 per share, taking the total proposed investment to Rs 16,756 crore.The agreement has been signed between Tata Steel and SG Tech Engineering Private Ltd (SG Spectra), an entity associated with APL Apollo's promoter group, according to a company statement.The proposed transactions are subject to regulatory approvals, which Tata Steel expects to secure in the coming months. The company aims to complete the entire transaction within the financial year 2026-27 (FY27).The acquisition is expected to strengthen Tata Steel's presence in the downstream steel products segment, particularly steel tubes and colour-coated products. APL Apollo will serve as a platform for Tata Steel to expand its downstream operations and drive growth in these segments.Under the proposed arrangement, the combined entity, APL Apollo Tubes Pvt Ltd, aims to build a production capacity of up to 15.5 million tonnes per annum (MTPA) by 2035. This will include 9 MTPA of steel tubes and 6.5 MTPA of colour-coated products.Tata Steel said the combination would help optimise capacity utilisation, unlock value, improve profitability and leverage the strengths of both companies.T V Narendran, CEO and managing director of Tata Steel, said: "We are very pleased to have entered into a comprehensive agreement with APL Apollo and the promoters as we create a downstream powerhouse for the future characterised by its inherent strengths of agility in the market, strong growth trajectory and benchmark capex-opex profile to serve the growing Indian market."This strategic move helps to consolidate the steel tubes and the colour coated business under Tata Steel's ownership while unlocking multiple synergies between the two companies. This will create value for all stakeholders with enhanced customer centricity, pan-India reach, and a full product portfolio. We look forward to working with our partners through this exciting journey."Tata Steel executive director and chief financial officer Koushik Chatterjee said the acquisition aligned with the company's strategy to expand its presence in value-added steel products through organic and inorganic growth.He said: "We have, over the last year, emphasised our strategic intent to grow aggressively in the value-added space and expand our downstream footprint both organically and inorganically. While we have multiple projects under construction in value-added segments like tin plate and hot-rolled, pickled and galvanised lines, APL Apollo presented a unique opportunity for us."
Article Summary: Tata Steel to acquire 26.6% stake in APL Apollo for Rs 15,510 crore and launch a 26% open offer. The acquisition is expected to strengthen Tata Steel's presence in the downstream steel products segment, particularly steel tubes and colour- coated products.

Article Title: Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train corridor, India’s high-speed train project, achieves power milestone as 50-km Surat-Bilimora section is energised; Surat-Vapi operations deadline now stands at late 2027
Article Text:
The ministry has recently pushed back the target for launching Bullet Train services on the 100-km Surat-Vapi stretch. (Image for representative purpose only)

‘Energisation’ of India’s first bullet train corridor

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train corridor: India’s first bullet train corridor has achieved yet another milestone. The overhead electrical equipment that will supply power to trains on the Surat-Bilimora stretch of the 508-km Mumbai-Ahmedabad Bullet Train corridor has been successfully energised, the railway ministry announced on Saturday.The process will now move ahead in phases, with shorter stretches being energised one at a time.The Surat-Bilimora stretch covers around 50 km between the two stations, with the tracks running along an elevated viaduct. The route crosses four rivers by means of bridges and also includes a steel bridge spanning National Highway 53.The Surat-Vapi corridor is the first stretch of the bullet train or high-speed rail corridor that is expected to be operationalised in the second half of 2027."Energisation will be carried out progressively in smaller sections, under the close supervision of technical teams to ensure safety and compliance with prescribed procedures," a railway ministry press statement said.Alongside the development, the ministry issued a public safety warning asking residents, commuters, construction personnel and others in areas near the corridor to stay away from overhead electrical equipment.It also cautioned against touching these installations or carrying out any unauthorised activity near the section.Officials clarified that switching on the power supply does not indicate that the stretch is ready for passenger train services. However, they described the milestone as an important step towards making the section operational.The ministry has recently pushed back the target for launching Bullet Train services on the 100-km Surat-Vapi stretch. The deadline, initially set for August 2027, has been moved to the final quarter of 2027."The section comprises both Up and Down lines on the elevated alignment and marks an important advancement towards further testing activities for the project," the ministry said.The ministry said the Mumbai-Ahmedabad Bullet Train corridor uses an advanced 2 × 25 kV overhead traction system, a sophisticated electrification technology deployed in high-speed rail networks around the world.Power for the system will be drawn from the national grid through 14 traction substations (TSS) positioned at strategic points along the 508-km route. "The electrification network comprises 14 strategically located traction substations (TSS) along the 508-km corridor. These substations will receive power from the national grid and supply it to the overhead traction system used by high-speed trains," the ministry said.A centralised control centre will oversee the entire electrical network, enabling the system to be monitored for safe and dependable operation.To reduce noise reaching nearby areas, the viaduct has been fitted with around 94,000 noise barriers, officials said.
Article Summary: Overhead electrical equipment that will supply power to trains on the Surat- Bilimora stretch of the 508-km Mumbai-Ahmedabad Bullet Train corridor has been successfully energised. The process will now move ahead in phases, with shorter stretches being energised one at a time.

Article Title: Bisleri samples initially flagged 'unsafe', subsequent tests find them compliant: Report

Bisleri water samples found compliant after initial safety concerns

NEW DELHI: Bisleri International's packaged drinking water samples that were initially declared unsafe have been found compliant with food safety regulations in subsequent testing, a government source told Reuters on Monday.The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ) had earlier sanctioned prosecution against the company after a regulatory sample of its packaged drinking water was found to exceed prescribed bromate limits.Bisleri appealed against the findings, following which the sample was sent to a referral food laboratory. The laboratory also declared it unsafe after detecting polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), the regulator had said.The latest testing found the samples compliant with regulations, the government source informed Reuters.The regulator also recalled batches of Bisleri packaged water that had been found unsafe.Bisleri International said drinking water safety was a priority for the company and that it would cooperate with the regulator to address the matter through the appropriate process.FSSAI had also sanctioned prosecution against Vasant Masala Pvt Ltd, Tit-Bit Foods India Pvt Ltd, Mimansa Industries and Asha Confectionery.The regulator suspended the licences of Urmi Lifesciences LLP and Gaur Ayurvedic Store for non-compliance with food safety rules. It also ordered Asha Confectionery to recall its pre-packaged chocolate-filled cookies after they were found unsafe.The FFSAI has stepped up its scrutiny of food businesses and e-commerce companies intensifying its enforcement drive.
Article Summary: Bisleri International's packaged drinking water samples that were initially declared unsafe have been found compliant with food safety regulations. The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India had earlier sanctioned prosecution against the company. The latest testing found the samples compliant with regulations, the government source informed Reuters.

Article Title: Bisleri water samples declared 'unsafe' by food regulator; company responds
Article Text:
Bisleri says it will cooperate after FSSAI sanctions prosecution

Bisleri disputes laboratory findings

What FSSAI said about the sample

Four other food businesses face prosecution

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

FSSAI steps up enforcement

NEW DELHI: Packaged drinking water major Bisleri International Pvt Ltd on Monday maintained that its products remain safe for consumption, after the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ) sanctioned prosecution against the company over a sample of its packaged drinking water declared unsafe.“Drinking water safety is a priority for Bisleri. We maintain stringent quality controls of over 90 tests across our 10-step manufacturing process and will continue to cooperate with FSSAI to address the matter through the appropriate regulatory process. A trusted brand for years, Bisleri remains safe for consumption,” the company said.In a detailed media statement, Bisleri said the regulatory matter concerned a single batch manufactured in September 2025 at its Goa facility, one of 143 plants in its network. The company also said it had not received any official notice from the food regulator.“We are aware of recent media reports that the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has issued a notice to Bisleri. The matter dates back approximately 14 months, to a batch produced in September 2025 at Bisleri’s Goa manufacturing facility, one of 143 plants in our network,” the statement said.According to the company, the FSSAI collected six samples from its Goa facility on September 30, 2025.Initial tests found that five samples met all applicable standards, while the sixth recorded a bromate level of 12 micrograms per litre, against the prescribed limit of 10 micrograms per litre.Following an appeal by Bisleri on November 22, 2025, the sample was sent to a referral laboratory for further testing. The laboratory found the bromate level to be within the prescribed limit but separately detected polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs).Bisleri said the difference between the test results raised questions that required clarification. It subsequently arranged for the same sample to be tested independently at an FSSAI-approved laboratory, which also found the bromate level to be within the prescribed limit.The company said it submitted the independent test results to the FSSAI's Western Regional Office along with a formal letter dated February 2, 2026.“We submitted the independent test results to FSSAI’s Western Regional Office with a formal letter dated 2 February 2026. We received no further communication from FSSAI after that submission and understood the matter to be closed. To date, Bisleri has received no notice by email or in hard copy and has been unable to locate the reported notice on FSSAI’s website,” the company said.The company's statement followed the FSSAI's announcement that it had sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri over the packaged drinking water sample.In a social media post, the regulator said a sample of “Packaged Drinking Water (other than Mineral Water)” collected from the company's premises did not comply with prescribed bromate limits and was declared unsafe under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.After Bisleri appealed against the findings, the sample was sent to a referral food laboratory, which also declared it unsafe after detecting PAHs, the FSSAI said. The regulator said the findings established violations relating to unsafe food under the law, leading it to sanction prosecution against the company.The FSSAI has also sanctioned prosecution against four other food businesses: Vasant Masala Pvt Ltd, Tit-Bit Foods India Pvt Ltd, Mimansa Industries and Asha Confectionery.Separately, it suspended the licences of Urmi Lifesciences LLP and Gaur Ayurvedic Store over non-compliance with food safety rules. The regulator also ordered Asha Confectionery to recall its pre-packaged chocolate-filled cookies after they were found unsafe.The action comes amid stepped-up enforcement by the FSSAI against food business operators and e-commerce companies during the current calendar year. The regulator has also intensified scrutiny of energy drink and alcoholic beverage manufacturers.
Article Summary: Bisleri International Pvt Ltd maintains that its products remain safe for consumption. Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ) sanctioned prosecution against the company over a sample of its packaged drinking water declared unsafe. Four other food businesses face prosecution.

Article Title: JK Group's fifth gen leader Abhishek Singhania ventures into real estate
Article Text:
Abhishek had also founded JK Tech (formerly JK Technosoft Ltd) in 1994 where he is MD.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: One of India’s oldest business houses — the Singhania family-run JK Group — is venturing big time into real estate by using significant land parcels held by it in UP and other places. Deriving its name from founder Juggilal (J) Singhania and his son Kamlapat (K) Singhania, one branch of the JK Organisation family headed by Abhishek Singhania has ventured into real estate with an initial investment of Rs 965 crore on six hotel projects with 650 keys in five destinations to begin with. The overall topline will be over Rs 4,400 crore across residential, mixed-use and urban redevelopment segments.JK Cotton, which started a mill in Kanpur in 1921, was rechristened JK Urbanscapes in 2022 that’s headed by Abhishek whose grandfather Padmapat was one of Kamlapat’s three sons. “The family owns substantial land parcels across UP and some other states. In Kanpur alone, for instance, the mill site was spread over 50 acres. To begin with, we will develop six acres of the same in Kanpur that will see two hotels that will be managed by Taj Group, including a Taj and a Ginger; Taj residences (serviced by the hotel group) and other uses,” said JK Urbanscapes CMD Abhishek Singhania.The Kanpur Taj and Ginger are expected to open in 2030.Part of JK Organisation, JK Urbanscapes Developers Ltd (JKUDL) has tied up with Taj parent Indian Hotels Co Ltd (IHCL) and Minor Hotels. The sites identified are known for pilgrimage, leisure, heritage and urban markets in UP, Uttarakhand, Bihar, West Bengal and Haryana.“We do not plan to take debt for land (acquisition). The leverage will be essentially construction finance. We will fund through a mix of debts and internal accruals. We will infuse equity,” said Abhishek Singhania.JK Urbanscapes’ residential portfolio includes the ongoing 90-acre Emerald Gulistan plotted residential township in Kanpur. “In Gurugram, our Advait Senior Living project in partnership with Pioneer Urban comprises 164 residences with a dedicated focus on senior living within a purpose-planned residential community,” said Maneesh Mansingka, joint MD of JK Urbanscapes.The company’s hospitality portfolio include a 78-key hotel in Bodh Gaya; a 41-key Kamla Castle hotel in Mussoorie; a 70-key hotel in Darjeeling and a 200-key hotel and residences project in Dehradun.“We also exploring hotel developments in Rishikesh, Jaipur and Kota. Through partnerships with established hospitality operators, including IHCL and Minor Hotels under its Anantara brand, we aim to combine hospitality expertise with a development approach shaped by the character and demand drivers of each location,” Mansingka added.Abhishek had also founded JK Tech (formerly JK Technosoft Ltd) in 1994 where he is MD. His Jaykay Enterprises manufactures components and products for the defence and aerospace sectors. “Hospitality is seeing a big boom in India and we will be present in this area too,” he said.
Article Summary: JK Cotton, which started a mill in Kanpur in 1921, was rechristened JK Urbanscapes in 2022. Part of JK Organisation, JKUDL has tied up with Taj parent Indian Hotels Co Ltd (IHCL) and Minor Hotels.

Article Title: Gold falls 11% to Rs 1.21 lakh and silver plunges 16.2% to Rs 1.47 lakh in a week to over one-year lows; analysts warn prices may slide further as US inflation data and Federal Reserve rate signals sh

Comex gold futures lost $370.9, or 9.5%, during the week, ending at $3,515.4 per ounce.

Gold and silver prices crash

Gold, silver price outlook

Gold price crash to continue? Gold and silver prices could face further selling pressure next week after both metals slumped to their lowest levels in more than a year. Analysts have said that investors will watch US inflation figures and signals from the Federal Reserve for indications of where interest rates are headed.Markets will also track mid-month purchasing managers’ index (PMI) readings from major economies, followed by US gross domestic product (GDP) figures, housing market data and durable goods orders. Inflation data will be particularly important in determining expectations about the Fed’s monetary policy, analysts said.On the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX), December gold futures shed Rs 14,927, or 11%, over the past week, settling at Rs 1,21,778 per 10 grams. The contract touched a low not seen in more than a year.Gold was last traded at a comparable level on October 30, 2025, when its price stood at Rs 1,21,508 per 10 grams, according to a PTI report.Silver futures for December delivery recorded a steeper weekly decline, losing Rs 28,496, or 16.2%, and also falling to a more than one-year low. The metal was last quoted near these levels on November 3, 2025, at Rs 1,47,758 per kg.The downturn in precious metals was equally pronounced in overseas markets. Comex gold futures lost $370.9, or 9.5%, during the week, ending at $3,515.4 per ounce. Silver futures fared worse, dropping $8.05, or 16.4%, to settle at $41.07 per ounce.Pranav Mer, Senior Vice President, EBG -- Commodity & Currency Research at JM Financial Services Ltd, said the outlook for both precious metals remained subdued, with the ongoing decline likely to continue. He added that prices could fall further as investors evaluate fresh economic indicators and reassess the interest rate outlook.Explaining the decline in domestic gold prices , Jateen Trivedi, VP Research Analyst -- Commodity and Currency at LKP Securities, said, "MCX gold witnessed a sharp sell-off last week, declining 11 per cent. The ongoing corrective trend extended as profit booking intensified across international and domestic bullion markets,"He added that the fall in global gold prices, alongside an appreciation in the rupee, had deepened the weakness in domestic bullion. A stronger rupee has put additional pressure on MCX prices by lowering the landed cost of imported gold.Describing the scale of the decline, Mer said, "The sell-off on bullions accelerated last week with gold falling close to $3,500 and silver at $41, both ending with a weekly loss of about 10-15 per cent, respectively,"Statements by Federal Reserve officials signalling a more hawkish approach have undermined demand for precious metals, as investors factor in the possibility of interest rates remaining elevated. The widespread decline in artificial intelligence-linked stocks has added to the selling pressure.Silver has also been hit by weakness across the industrial metals segment, with copper and zinc recording particularly sharp declines, Mer pointed out.According to him, the sell-off in equities prompted investors to liquidate bullion holdings as well, while demand for safe-haven bonds increased.The US dollar continued to hold firm, moving towards the 104 level against a basket of major currencies. Comments from Fed officials have reinforced expectations that interest rates could stay high for an extended period.Mer said, "Inflation issue is not only in US, but across most other regions, including India and we may see rate hike coming there as well. The Fed fund future are pricing in 96 per cent chance of a 25-basis-points rate hike in December,"On the geopolitical front, efforts to resolve the conflicts involving Iran and Ukraine have made little headway. Talks mediated by the US between Iran and other parties have stalled, while the outcome of last week's meeting involving Washington, Beijing and Moscow on the Ukraine conflict remains uncertain.Global bullion markets could see sharper price swings in the coming week as the Thanksgiving holiday in the US will shorten the trading week and leave markets with lower liquidity.In India, commodity markets will remain shut during the morning trading session on Tuesday for Guru Nanak Jayanti.
Article Summary: Comex gold futures lost $370.9, or 9.5%, during the week, ending at $3,515.4 per ounce. On the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX), December gold futures shed Rs 14,927, or 11%, over the past week, settling at Rs 1,21,778 per 10 grams.
